The excerpts show `batch_server` (TID 627449) on CPU 3 waking `flusher` (TID 627455) and workers through futex operations. These samples don’t show an obviously long `batch_server` syscall or a worker blocked for a long interval on a lock.

But the trace has no lock-acquire/contention events or lock-owner information, and most events between the sampled windows are omitted. Futex activity alone doesn’t establish that a lock is held too long—or even identify which futexes correspond to locks.

To check, capture lock contention/acquire/release events (or use `perf lock`) alongside complete scheduler wakeup/switch events for the relevant interval. If contention is confirmed, profile the critical section; typical fixes are to shorten it, avoid I/O or sleeping while holding the lock, or replace a shared lock with per-worker state or queues.
